Stn_Des:
Velocity-Area station, 22m-wide channel in urban setting. Gauge is located just upstream of V-Weir on the left bank of the River Suir behind Thurles Leisure Centre.

There have been several changes to the river channel near this gauge over the years, and the gauge itself has moved more than once. These events have added uncertainty to flow estimation as the rating curve characteristics have not remained constant over time.

Gaugings are available to download back to 1946 but continuous estimated flow data are currently only published from 1984 onwards. There was a change in flow hydrograph from October 1984 linked to channel work that lowered the river bed and changed the control at that time.

Ratings since 1984 are validated to 0.97*QMED. Overall there is high uncertainty in flow estimation since 2008 due to a lack of regular gaugings with the largest gap in the gauging record from 2008 to 2014. Flow measurements typically taken downstream of the gauge between the weir and the pedestrian bridge 200m downstream. There is seasonality evident at lower levels with summer/winter ratings between 1984 and 2000 implemented to improve accuracy.

Station 16002 Beakstown, which is approximately 7km downstream on the Suir is a better flow estimation site with a longer published flow record. The Drish River and some minor tributaries flow into the River Suir between the two stations.

Drone footage available.

Bridge

Channel Width: 17m

Channel Conditions:
Upstream, left bank: Grass bank, some minor development before the gauge.
Upstream, right bank: Overhanging trees.
Downstream, left bank: Overhanging trees.
Downstream, right bank: Grass bank

Station Limitations:
Gap in gaugings from 2001 to 2018.

Highest Flow Measurements:
01/03/1978: 49.070 cumec at 1.600m

24/03/1964: 34.910 cumec at 1.122m

Extreme caution advised over flood flows please take note of the reliable limit for the time period (see AMAX table), bridge prone to blockages with trees and AMAX flow estimates may be overestimated.

Gauge installed to provide real time data on the Dargle and to support post flood relief scheme monitoring. Velocity-Area station, 11.5m wide, trees on the left bank, small amount of vegetation on right bank then clear flat field. There is a sharp bend 100m d/s and a multi arch bridge 300m d/s. This site has a “flashy” flow regime. Current rating validated to 37.7m3/s for flow estimation up 2m, after which there is uncertainty.
HYD_DIS_DES: Hydrometric Description Primary Flow Control: Channel Other Controls Possibly Affecting Flows: Sharp bend 100m d/s Multi arch bridge 300m d/s Bank Full Level: 2m Channel Width: 11.5m Station Limitations: Tree noted to have fallen in d/s on 09/01/2025. On 21/07/2025 an excavator diverted the river into a 2.2m wide channel 30m downstream of the station. The excavator did this as it was removing a large beech tree which was partially in the water at the bend of in the river downstream of the station. The channel was reinstated on 22/07/2026 and looks to have returned the channel to as was, but further flow measurement will confirm if there is a slight change in control. Highest Flow Measurements: 2 gaugings on 15/11/2025 1.92m-2.03m All gauged flows have been in bank to date. Flow Record Description: Max level reached since the gauge was installed in 2021 is estimated to be 3.1m occurring in Jan 2026 (logger was over topped).
RATING_SUMMARY: Good rating to 1.34m (15.23m3/s), fair rating to 2m (37.73m3/s) and extrapolated above this level. Max level reached since the gauge installed was in 2021 estimated to be 3.1m in Jan 2026 (logger was over topped).

ObjectDescription: Velocity area station located upstream of multi arch bridge. Rock bed. Negligible weed growth. Bridge downstream thought to act as a control at high flow.
Stn_Des:
Velocity-Area station, 13m wide with relatively small amounts of vegetation on both banks. This site has a “flashy” flow regime. Current rating validated to 0.78*QMED for good flow estimation up 2.5m, after which there is some uncertainty. The bridge 15m downstream is prone to blockages. Drainage works were carried from 1957 to 1961.

Station Limitations:
Bridge prone to blockage with trees washed downstream.

Rating Curve Information:
Good rating to 0.78*QMed. Some uncertainty above 2.5m. Bridge just d/s prone to debris blockages.

Highest Flow Measurements:
6 gaugings on 25/08/2020 1.89m-2.91m

Flow Record Description: Only gauged at a high level on 25/08/2020, relationship assumed similar back through the record.
Details of bypassing floods - field upstream left bank floods and there is a possible flow path to bypass the gauge through flood arches in the field on left bank.
Gauge relocated from bridge to current location in July 2004.

Drone footage available.

Rating retrospectively changed back through the record in 2021 on account of gaugings captured in August 2020.

This ex-EPA gauge is located on the right bank approximately 15m downstream of the R362 road bridge. Staff gauge installed on weir containment wall, left bank. It was taken over by the OPW in October 2023 to help quantify the inflows into Lough Funshinagh along with the 26405 Rahara gauge. 

Velocity-area station with nonstandard flat-v steel weir acting as control. There is no flow over the weir when the staff gauge is at or below 0.137m. The weir drowns out at 0.4m and the channel may backwater due to excessive weed growth downstream. There was a poor understating of flow dynamics within the channel and gaugings taken prior to 2020 were of poor quality. No reliable rating curve could be developed prior to 2020. There are also gaps in the gauging record (for example no gaugings were taken from November 2002 to January 2008).
The station provides an alert before the embankments are at risk of over topping in times of high water levels in the reservoir.

Velocity-Area station, 20m wide. This site has a “flashy” flow regime. Bankfull level approx 1.5m, resulting in significant out of bank flow upstream and downstream of the station.
